gp.heading: Cost of Revenue and Gross Profit
gp.text: Cost of revenue for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $0 as compared to $27,016 for the three months ended September 30, 2025, a decrease of $27,016. This decrease was attributable to our decision to shift our focus away from our colorectal cancer screening business in February 2026. As a result, gross profit decreased by $102,162.

cor.heading: Cost of Revenue
cor.text: The Company’s cost of revenue for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $873,243 compared to nil for the three months ended September 30, 2025. This increase was the result of the Arcade Acquisition. Cost of revenue included raw materials, labor and overhead necessary to produce the products sold and shipped during the three months ended September 30, 2026.

rd.heading: Research and Development Expenses
rd.text: Research and development expenses for the three months ended September 30, 2026 were $1,255,029 compared to $39,318 for the three months ended September 30, 2025, an increase of $1,215,711. This increase was primarily the result of increases in share-based compensation of $0.5 million and professional and consulting fees of $0.3 million, both related to the build-out of the Bridgeport facility and the Quantum Drones business, as well as technology expense of $0.25 million representing the amortization of prepaid technical support under our BP United license agreement, and $0.1 million of amortization of the BP United drone technology license.

sm.heading: Sales and Marketing Expenses
sm.text: Sales and marketing expenses for the three months ended September 30, 2026, were $771,150 compared to $434,827 for the three months ended September 30, 2025, an increase of $336,323. This increase was primarily related to increased professional and consulting fees of $0.5 million, including share-based compensation, and office expenses of $0.1 million in support of the planned launch of our Quantum Drones business, partially offset by a $0.3 million decrease in marketing and advertising expenses following our pivot in focus from the colorectal cancer business.

ga.heading: General and Administrative Expenses
ga.text: General and administrative expenses for the three months ended September 30, 2026 were $2,929,422 compared to $692,590 for the three months ended September 30, 2025, an increase of $2,236,832. The increased expenses were primarily the result of increases in share-based compensation of $0.4 million and professional and consulting fees of $1.3 million, both related to the recruitment of the management team and staffing for our Quantum Drones business, $0.4 million related to increased overhead related to our Bridgeport facility and corporate offices in Connecticut, and $0.1 million of acquisition-related costs and insurance related to the Arcade Acquisition.

nonop.text: Other expense, net for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $58,158 compared to $41,299 for the three months ended September 30, 2025, resulting in increased other expenses of $16,859. This increase was primarily the result of a $250,000 accrual for the settlement of an outstanding legal dispute with Boustead Securities, LLC, partially offset by $125,000 of escrow funds returned to the Company under the July 24, 2026 amendment of the APA and PSA, increased other income and decreased interest expense for the three months ended September 30, 2026 compared to the same period in 2025.

ocf.heading: Cash Flows from Operating Activities
ocf.text: For the nine months ended September 30, 2026, cash flows used in operating activities were $9,731,639 compared to $3,157,192 used during the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The increase in cash flows used in operating activities of $6,574,447 was primarily the result of increased losses resulting from the investment in operating expenses and working capital to fund the ramp-up of our Quantum Drones business, the operations of Arcade Technology, as well as severance costs related to our shift from our colorectal cancer business.

sbc.text: These estimates had a significant effect on our results for the nine months ended September 30, 2026, including $3.3 million of acquired in-process research and development expense attributable to ordinary shares issued for the Project LightShift license and $3.2 million of share-based compensation for shares issued or issuable to non-employees for services. We also capitalized $5.5 million for the BP United license, which was paid in ordinary shares.

wc.heading: Working Capital Discussion
wc.text:
We have incurred significant recurring losses from operations and negative operating cash flows. As of September 30, 2026, we have an accumulated deficit totaling $126.4 million, cash on hand of $4.9 million, and working capital of $6.3 million. During the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the Company incurred a net loss of approximately $21.5 million.

Historically, the Company has relied upon equity transactions and loans from third parties to fund operations. We plan to fund our cash flow and working capital needs through current cash on hand and future debt and/or equity financings which we may obtain through one or more public or private equity offerings, debt financings, government or other third-party funding, strategic alliances or collaboration agreements. The Company’s failure to do so could have a material and adverse effect upon its operations and its shareholders. Management’s plans may also include reducing or deferring certain discretionary expenditures and pursuing strategic partnerships and/or revenue-generating contracts; however, there can be no assurance these plans will be effectively implemented or be successful. During the nine months ended September 30, 2026, the Company received $6.0 million in proceeds from the Investment as described above and received proceeds from the exercise of outstanding warrants of $15.2 million.

capex.text: During the nine months ended September 30, 2026, cash flows used in investing activities were $4,916,479 compared to $400,000 used during the nine months ended September 30, 2025. The increase in cash flows used in investing activities of $4,516,479 is primarily the result of cash used to fund the Arcade Acquisition, including the assets and the Bridgeport facility, land and machinery used for that business, which was $4.2 million, as well as the final $0.5 million payment for our pancreatic cancer screening intellectual property license, $0.1 million of purchases of property and equipment, and $0.1 million of purchases of marketable securities.

net sales.heading: Revenue
net sales.text: The Company’s revenue for the three months ended September 30, 2026 was $966,833 compared to nil for the three months ended September 30, 2025. This increase was solely attributable to the sales at Arcade Technology, subsequent to the Acquisition Date, of precision metal stamping products across three product lines: electrical components, tooling, and general metal stamping products, along with related manufactured components and assemblies, to customers across a variety of industries.

intro.text: Historically, we have developed and sold in-vitro diagnostic (“IVD”) tests for the early detection of cancer. In March 2025, we acquired a license from Liquid Bioscience, Inc. to access a portfolio of novel mRNA biomarkers and AI developed proprietary algorithm, for the non-invasive detection of pancreatic cancer with a blood test. We have an exclusive license to develop such a test using these biomarkers and algorithm with the unilateral option to acquire them. We are also developing a product candidate called PancAlert, a stool-based screening test aimed at detecting pancreatic cancer. We have received non-refundable government grant income to cover a percentage of the PancAlert project-related costs.

lines.name: Cash and cash equivalents
lines.why: Cash can repay debt or be paid out: a financial asset. Cash needed to run the business is operating; move it if you know how much.

lines.name: Receivables
lines.why: Owed by customers for sales: operating.

lines.name: Prepaid and other current assets
lines.why: Prepayments and other operating items: operating.

lines.name: Property, plant and equipment
lines.why: Assets used to produce and sell: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease right-of-use assets
lines.why: Leased stores, offices and equipment used in the business: operating.

lines.name: Intangible assets
lines.why: Acquired technology, brands and customer relationships: operating.

lines.name: Equity-method investments
lines.why: Stakes in associated businesses, usually part of operations. Financial if held as an investment.

lines.name: Accounts payable
lines.why: Owed to suppliers for operations: operating.

lines.name: Accrued liabilities
lines.why: Services and other costs not yet paid: operating.

lines.name: Operating lease liabilities
lines.why: Rent owed on leases used in the business: operating by default. Move it to financing to treat leases like debt (if the balance sheet has no lease line of its own, they sit inside other liabilities).

lines.name: Lease liabilities
lines.why: IFRS 16 puts every lease on the balance sheet like a loan for the asset: financial.

lines.name: Deferred tax liabilities
lines.why: Taxes on operating income deferred: operating.

lines.name: Other current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current assets minus the current lines above: current assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current assets, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current assets (total assets − current assets) minus the non-current lines above: assets the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Total current liabilities minus the current lines above: current liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.

lines.name: Other non-current liabilities, not tagged separately
lines.why: Non-current liabilities (total liabilities − current liabilities) minus the non-current lines above: liabilities the company tags its own way. Operating by default.
